details.description: GPT-5.4 is OpenAI's reasoning model for complex professional work, released March 5, 2026 as OpenAI's most token-efficient reasoning model to date. It combines frontier coding ability with general reasoning and was the first general-purpose OpenAI model released with native computer-use capabilities, letting agents operate applications via mouse, keyboard and code libraries like Playwright. It takes text and image input and produces text-only output, with configurable reasoning effort (none, low, medium, high, xhigh) and a knowledge cutoff of August 31, 2025. OpenAI has since released GPT-5.5 (April 2026) and GPT-5.6 as newer flagship models, though GPT-5.4 remains available via the API.
advantages: Scores 83.0% on GDPval, OpenAI's benchmark of economically valuable professional tasks, up from 70.9% for GPT-5.2 (OpenAI).
Scores 75.0% on OSWorld-Verified, a computer-use benchmark, up from 47.3% for GPT-5.2 (OpenAI).
Scores 93.7% on ARC-AGI-1, up from 86.2% for GPT-5.2 (OpenAI).
OpenAI reports individual factual claims are 33% less likely to be false than GPT-5.2's (OpenAI).
A tool-search feature that OpenAI reports cuts token usage by 47% when working with large tool ecosystems (OpenAI).
disadvantages: OpenAI reports long-context performance degrades significantly beyond 256,000 tokens (OpenAI).
Output is text-only; the model does not generate images, audio or video (OpenAI API model docs).
Knowledge cutoff of August 31, 2025 (OpenAI API model docs).
Superseded as OpenAI's flagship chat model by GPT-5.5, released in April 2026, and later GPT-5.6, though still available via the API (OpenAI, Wikipedia).
use_cases: Professional knowledge work across spreadsheets, presentations and documents
Agentic coding, including complex frontend development
Computer-use agents that operate applications end to end
Tool-calling agents working with large tool ecosystems

sources.title: GPT-5.4 (xhigh) - Intelligence, Performance & Price Analysis | Artificial Analysis

notes: OpenAI's own announcement post (openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-5-4/) returned HTTP 403 on a direct fetch, so it was read via a read-only proxy (r.jina.ai) of the same URL; the cited source URL is the original openai.com page. OpenAI's API docs page states a 1,050,000-token context window, matching the higher of the catalog's two max_input_tokens facts (1,000,000 and 1,050,000); not flagged as a conflict. OpenAI's API docs page lists Chat Completions, Responses and Batch as supported endpoints, matching the catalog's facts. Not deprecated per OpenAI's own deprecations page (checked directly) or its API docs; description says 'superseded' only in the sense that GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6 are now OpenAI's newer flagship models, not that GPT-5.4 has been withdrawn.
